newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica shares welcome possible BT deal.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica shares welcome possible BT deal.

text.p: Telefonica shares gained ground on Wednesday as jitters over low connection fees for the second operator faded away and a likely international alliance boosted hopes for the Spanish telecoms giant, analysts and traders said.
"It seems Telefonica shares are bouncing back from sharp recent losses, but it's too early to make forecasts while there's still nothing official," one analyst said.
At around 1349 GMT Telefonica shares were up 40 pesetas to 3,390, outperforming the Ibex-35 index of leading shares.
After a tame recovery yesterday, with a 0.4 percent gain, Telefonica shares were recovering from an accumulated loss on Friday and Monday of 5.2 percent.
"If the reports of a strategic alliance with British Telecom are confirmed, it would be good for Telefonica," said an expert.

U.K. newspaper The Financial Times reported on Wednesday that BT was currently negotiating a stake in Telefonica International (TISA), which has holdings in South American countries including Argentina, Chile and Peru.
Up to now, the firm's current pan-European joint venture, Unisorce, is providing less than impressive results.
"Telefonica has not had much from Unisorce, with its balance sheet still in the red," an analyst observed.
Telefonica has a 25 percent stake in Unisource, which is also owned by Sweden's Telia, Swiss Telecom and Holland's KPN.
In the first nine months of 1996 Unisorce posted a loss of 22.018 billion pesetas.

"A deal with BT, with them entering TISA makes a lot of sense. Telefonica can open the door to Latin America for BT, while BT, through MCI, would be the right Telefonica partner for the U.S. business" an analyst commented.

In the meantime the market had started to digest the possibility of government compensation if, as seems likely, Telefonica charges the second domestic phone operator Retevision a lower-than-anticipated connection charge for using its network.

According to unconfirmed local press reports, the long distance domestic connection fee would be between 2.0 and 2.5 pesetas per minute in line with Retevision's proposal, but far from Telefonica's proposed 7.0 pesetas.
To offset this, the recently-privatised Telefonica could increase its fixed line rental fee to its 16 million clients.
"That would increase Telefonica's income by around 18 billion pesetas, which would compensate for the low connection charges," said an analyst.
On Tuesday Spain's Development Ministry said it would announce the much-awaited fees for connection to Telefonica's networks later this week.
Telefonica has 16.3 million lines in Spain from which it earned 1.4 trillion pesetas last year, not including earnings from international phone traffic.
